chapter: Small's Paradise, Fletcher Henderson and Horace
title: Horace Henderson's treatment of Fletcher, and his absence at the funeral
summary: Horace borrowed Fletcher's car, took his music and was missing at the funeral; Dance later found him playing a hotel lounge in Colorado.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: But I mean what you were saying about Horace was --

Horace just treated Fletcher so bad when he came here. He brought a little group here from out of -- from out of Ohio. And Fletcher, you know, he was a good piano player, and Fletcher would loan him his car, would run off with Fletcher's car, and he stole a lot of themusic and all like that. And the saddest thing of it was, after Fletcher had passed, they had Fletcher's funeral down at Mother AME Zion Church on 137th Street and 7th Avenue, one of the oldest Negro churches in the state of New York City because they came from way out of around town, and we were there that day, and John Hammond was there. All musicians (unintelligible) was there.

And we were looking for Horace. Didn't show up. So John Hammond said 'Hop, can you see Horace? I say, well, this is funny. (unintelligible). I'm looking to see if I can see him, but he wasn't there. Nobody see him.

Well, you know, I've often heard people say this about Horace, but I've never -- I mean I never knew what it was about him, I mean what's wrong with him, because he'd go back and work with Fletcher and everything.
He's a good piano player, a good musician.
Yeah, but it looked as though
Fletcher would always forgive him, because --
(Simultaneous remarks)
Yeah, he was that way. Cruel --
: I mean what actually did he do wrong. I mean did he cheat him?
(Simultaneous remarks)
-- take the music, take the car and run off, you know.
: Oh, sort of like irresponsible and selfish. I see. Yeah, I mean I've heard that before, but I --
That's true.
-- never really -- I've heard people say, well, he was bad news, and I mean John Hammond told me that too.
Johnny's right. He ain't lying either.

: But, you know, it's a funny thing because I saw him last year. He was -- we worked the Broadmoor Hotel in Colorado, great, big, beautiful hotel, and it was some white guy with an Italian name had a quartet in the coffee shop. And my wife and I were having breakfast or something. She said -- no, of course, that was in the evening. She said, let's just have a little snack. I think we were going to one of these jazz things. Said, 'that looks like Horace Henderson', and he's sitting there. They're just

playing nothing, you know, just playing dance tunes, and people are eating, nobody paying attention. It was Horace. And he's living up there with his wife, and they have -- we talked to him. They have two, three horses, and he looked in great shape, you know.
He's in great shape.

Helen says, aren't you going to play anything? So he said, sure, and he played. So in the next number he played two, three choruses, and it was very good, you know, a little more -- he used to play like Earl, but now he plays more like Teddy Wilson. But it's a strange story.
Yes, very true.
Because he had a lot of talent.
Very lot of talent, could arrange. Very good arranger, very good musician.
Well, why would he want to take Fletcher's music when he could write his own, just laziness?
Oh, just (unintelligible) brothers --
